standard_prerequisites.name: The basic open D(f) as the set of primes not containing f
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the start of both displayed computations (lines 4004-4008 and 4020-4024)
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the two basic opens in terms of membership of the idempotent in the prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: Values of an idempotent in residue fields
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the end of both computations (lines 4009-4017 and 4025-4032)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns non-membership into being equal to 1 modulo the prime and membership into being 0, which makes the two pieces complementary.

core_obligations: Rewrite D(e) as the set of primes where e is nonzero in the residue field, which for an idempotent means e equals 1 there (proof lines 4003-4017).
Rewrite D(1-e) in the same way, obtaining the primes where e equals 0 (proof lines 4018-4033).
Conclude that the two sets are disjoint and cover the spectrum, since the image of the idempotent in any residue field is either 1 or 0 (proof lines 4034-4035).
proof_roadmap: Describe both basic opens through the value of e in the residue fields (proof lines 4000-4033).
Use that an idempotent in a field is 0 or 1 to get the disjoint covering (proof lines 4034-4036).
difficulty_reason: For an idempotent e of a ring R the lemma states that the spectrum decomposes as the disjoint union of the two basic opens D(e) and D(1-e) (statement lines 3991-3998). The proof does not argue with the Zariski topology directly: it rewrites each of the two basic opens as the set of primes where the image of the idempotent in the residue field takes the value 1, respectively 0, using that an idempotent in a domain is 0 or 1, and then observes that these two conditions are complementary (proof lines 4000-4036). Passing to residue fields is what makes the two pieces visibly disjoint and covering, and the author writes both chains out. H2.
